governance.architecture_and_history: Bliss GVS Pharma Limited, incorporated in 1984 as Bliss Chemicals and Pharmaceuticals India, is a Mumbai-headquartered pharmaceutical company with over 40 years of industrial expertise. It specializes in the development, manufacturing, and marketing of high-quality pharmaceutical formulations, particularly excelling in suppositories and pessaries, where it is among the world's largest manufacturers by volume. The company is listed on both the BSE and NSE. Key milestones include the launch of its flagship product 'Today' – Vaginal Contraceptive in 1986, and continuous expansion of its global presence, exporting to over 60 countries with a strong market position in Sub-Saharan Africa. The company operates manufacturing facilities certified by global regulatory bodies such as EU GMP, US FDA, and WHO GMP, including facilities in Palghar and Daman, and two units in Nigeria. Its R&D center in Mumbai is recognized by the DSIR (Government of India). In Q4 FY2025, Bliss GVS commissioned an additional 2.5 MW solar capacity to enhance energy resilience. A significant recent event is the proposed acquisition of a controlling stake (approximately 43.28%) by Anupam Rasayan India Ltd for ₹1,369 Crore in May 2026, which also triggered a mandatory open offer for an additional 26% stake from public shareholders. This acquisition is aimed at strengthening Anupam Rasayan's presence across the pharmaceutical value chain.

operations.revenue_value_chain: Bliss GVS Pharma operates on a branded generic business model, specializing in pharmaceutical dosage forms such as suppositories, pessaries, tablets, capsules, and ointments. The company's core revenue streams are derived from selling its own branded and generic medicines, as well as contract manufacturing for other pharmaceutical companies like Sun Pharma, Mankind, Sanofi, and Alkem. It occupies a mid-position in the pharmaceutical value chain, focusing on formulation, production, and packaging rather than drug discovery. A significant portion of its revenue is export-oriented, with the African region accounting for approximately 65% of consolidated revenues in FY2025, rising to about 74% in 9M FY2026. The anti-malarial segment alone contributes around a third of its revenues, making it sensitive to malaria incidence. The company's niche focus on rectal and vaginal dosage forms differentiates it from many generic drug makers. Consolidated revenue for FY2025-26 was ₹92,711.28 lakh, up from ₹80,972.62 lakh year-over-year.
